saints.name: St. Philip Neri
saints.title: Priest
saints.shortBlurb: The joyful “Apostle of Rome” and founder of the Oratory, who won souls through cheerfulness and charity…
biography: Born at Florence in 1515, Philip was educated by the Dominicans of San Marco. Sent at eighteen to a rich uncle at San Germano to learn trade, he underwent a sudden conversion, and in 1533 went to Rome, where for seventeen years he lived as a layman, nursing the sick and speaking of God with workmen in the streets.

In 1548 he founded the Confraternity of the Most Holy Trinity of Pilgrims and Convalescents, and in 1551 was ordained priest, dwelling at San Girolamo della Carita. His evening gatherings of prayer, readings, and song, for which Palestrina composed music and from which the oratorio takes its name, grew into the Congregation of the Oratory, approved by Pope Gregory XIII in 1575 at Santa Maria in Vallicella, the Chiesa Nuova.

Cheerful, blunt, and tender with penitents, he became so beloved in the city that he was called the Apostle of Rome. He died on 26 May 1595 and was canonized by Pope Gregory XV in 1622 on the same day as Ignatius of Loyola, Francis Xavier, Teresa of Avila, and Isidore the Farmer. Because of his unfailing gaiety in holiness, he is honoured as a patron of joy.
saints.knownFor: The joyful Apostle of Rome and founder of the Oratory.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 26 May
